title: [SSH] add multisession decryption and REKEY decryption support
description:
Hi  

This merge request to address 2 issues on SSH decryption.  

## ISSUE 1) no-multi session in live decryption

Currently multi session decryption within the same capture process using TShark don't work.  
See issue : https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20574  


## ISSUE 2) decryption failed after ssh REKEY

Thus, traffic decryption don't work after SSH REKEY occurs.   
See issue : https://gitlab.com/wireshark/wireshark/-/issues/20575



This merge request to solve both issues (live and offline decryption work now).  


## THIS MERGE REQUEST SOLVED ISSUE 1 + 2: 

**All captures and traces of the issue had been provides directly in the issues.**  

**Here will only be posted a final capture where multiple sessions + multiple REKEY occurs and decryption is working fine on all frames.**     

### Captures:  

#### Capture command

```bash
/usr/src/build/wireshark/build/run/tshark \
        -i enp0s3 \
        -n \
        -o ssh.keylog_file:/home/nba/no-multi.keylog \
        -o ssh.desegment_buffers:TRUE \
        -o tcp.desegment_tcp_streams:TRUE \
        -o tcp.reassemble_out_of_order:TRUE \
        -t ad \
        -l \
        -f 'host 10.0.50.78 and (host 10.0.50.77 or host 10.0.50.75) and port 22' \
        -T fields \
        -e frame.number \
        -e frame.time_relative \
        -e ip.src \
        -e ip.dst \
        -e tcp.srcport \
        -e tcp.dstport \
        -e tcp.len \
        -e _ws.col.Protocol \
        -e _ws.col.Info  \
        -e ssh.cookie \
        -o ssh.debug_file:/home/nba/no-multi.debug \
        -w tssh1.pcapng
        -e ssh.message_code \
        -e ssh.payload \
        --log-level noisy \
        --log-domain packet-ssh 
        -w no-multi.pcap


```

#### Test command

- for multi sessions: 

```bash
/usr/src/build/openssh-portable/ssh -F none -o KexAlgorithms=mlkem768x25519-sha256 -o Ciphers=chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com  nba@10.0.50.77 ls / 2>&1 >/dev/null
```
and   
```bash
/usr/src/build/openssh-portable/ssh -F none -o KexAlgorithms=mlkem768x25519-sha256 -o Ciphers=chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com  nba@10.0.50.75 ls / 2>&1 >/dev/null
```

- for REKEY:  
```bash
/usr/src/build/openssh-portable/ssh -F none -o KexAlgorithms=mlkem768x25519-sha256 -o Ciphers=chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com  -o RekeyLimit=1K nba@10.0.50.77 du -a /var/log/ 2>&1 >/dev/null
```


### Capture: 

Using mlkem768x25519-sha256/sntrup761x25519-sha512 + chacha20-poly1305 (also working with other algorithms + ciphers) :

mentioned in issue #20575

This is not memory safe, you don't check that `pinfo->num` is less than `MAX_FRAMES`.

You should not use an array like this anyway, it's very wasteful of memory; even if you need a copy of data for every frame, you only need a copy for frames that are in the conversation, not every frame in the capture. You should use a different data structure.

You can store information about individual frames with `p_add_proto_data`, in epan/proto_data.h  You can also store data about individual frames in a `wmem_tree_t`. The latter can be useful if what you really need to store is state transitions (like what frames REKEYs occur, and where a lot of information is the same for every frame after a REKEY until the next one), as you can use `wmem_tree_lookup32_le` to look up the node in the tree for the index less than equal to the current index, e.g. you can look up `pinfo->num` and find the node corresponding to the most reset REKEY frame.

> The sequence_number is initialized to zero for the first packet, and is incremented after every packet (regardless of whether encryption or MAC is in use).  **It is never reset, even if keys/algorithms are renegotiated later.**

It is probably better to store all the data from the keylog file into memory upon first encountering ssh, rather than rewinding the file and reading it again. That is what TLS does. Somewhat more complicated of a change that could perhaps be done later.

The issue here is not about data which are already in the keylog during the first session but about a new couple of cookie + shared_secret which is registred later while the new session arrived during the first session (and its encryption contexte) and is mixed with it.  
`rewind` is a simple way to catch new strings in the keylog.
From my understanding you asked that I refresh from memory but not from file so I can change for something else but if you can please provide a way to get new string from memory without scanning the file again or an example.   
Thanks :smile:

Having a look at TLS (packet-tls.c) show that the keylog file is processed in the early routing and during the handshake and from the first switch case which route packet in the dissector and is reprocessed each time a packet is routed or a switched to a ((HandshakeType) msg_type).   

In SSH (specially in packet-ssh.c), keylog is only called and analyzed after all routing of the packet had been done and only on SERVER REPLY after routing from `kex_specific_dissector()` to the function which parsed keys for the selected algorithm => keylog is not arbitrary reprocessed after any KEXINIT or at any pass through `ssh_dissect_ssh2()` or `ssh_dissect_key_echange()`    

So maybe I did not understand what you asked (and why) but from my understanding it's not relevant here in the context of this SSH dissector without a complete rewrite (and new design) of the SSH dissector in `packet-ssh.c`

NB:   
I can precise in comment that this instruction is necessary for live flow decryption of any new session arriving while another had already been captured in TShark because ssh dissector design don't rescan keylog on each KEXINIT or on each routing decision inside the dissector but only after parsing KEX_algo-xxx_REPLY.   

Please let me know and / or explane more what I need to do as I maybe had misunderstand your request

`ssh_dissect_key_exchange` is designed to dissect an unencrypted entire SSH packet. Calling it here creates an odd and incorrect nested tree (which also has an expert info):

![image](/uploads/1d77bed98e0dbe6dc19e9bdb7bddf69d/image.png)

The functions need to be changed in some manner. Doing that could also dramatically simplify or eliminate the per packet metadata that you're storing. From what I understand, nearly the entire point of that is to undo how `ssh_dissect_key_exchange` updates the frames where the first KEX was seen, because that marks the end of the unencrypted packets. Presumably it would be simpler to only set `peer_data->frame_key_start` and `peer_data->frame_key_end` when dissecting the initial unencrypted key exchange that begins a session, but not set it at all on a REKEY (and then you wouldn't have to unset it.) All it is used for is to decide whether to call `ssh_dissect_key_exchange` or `ssh_try_dissect_encrypted_packet` at the start of a packet.

You also do not need to tell `ssh_dissect_key_exchange` to desegment here, because desegmentation has already been taken care of in this function.

OK I will see what I can do.

NEWKEYS packet in REKEY are not formed as first NEWKEYS packet.   
Here total decrypted length = 12 =>    
+ 4 length_prefix (value 8)
+ 1 msg_code value 21(10) (also = payload)    
+ 1 padding_length (value 6)    
+ 6 padding_string      
So it respect RFC as it is 12+ bytes BUT the four bytes length_prefix say that the length is 8 (1 msg_code + 1 padding_length=6 + 6 padding_string).    

During rekey, total decrypted length = 12 including length_prefix which don't seems to be the case on other NEWKEYS frames which don't included the prefixed length in the total computed packet length ( newkeys out of REKEY sequence).   

![newkey_rekey](/uploads/0910ecc3c594c1d17be2018e35805c8f/newkey_rekey.png)


### Is OpenSSH violating the spec?   
from my understanding it stay 100% compliant with RFC 4253 - Section 6 (Binary Packet Protocol) which said:    
> The minimum size of a packet is 16 (or the cipher block size, whichever is larger).   
But it said too:     
>>The minimum value for packet_length is 1 (payload length) + 4 (minimum padding) + 1 (padding_length byte) = 6,
and with packet_length (4 bytes) added = 10 bytes.
>However, since the packet must be a multiple of the cipher block size (typically 8 or 16), padding is added to align the total length accordingly.   


The rule that "minimum size is 16 bytes" seems to be enforced on the encrypted (wire) format, not after decryption.
And once decrypted, the packet length field can be as small as 8, so the decrypted packet can be as small as 12 bytes total.   

So I think that making an arbitrary check on packet_length to 12 bytes without the 4 bytes length prefixed seems to not handle all cases and specially when a REKEY occurs.

> The rule that "minimum size is 16 bytes" seems to be enforced on the encrypted (wire) format, not after decryption.

Perhaps, but in the particular case ChaCha20 is a stream cipher, and has> no block size, so the encrypted (wire) size is also 12 bytes total (not including the Poly1305 MAC).

The RFC says:

> Note that the length of the concatenation of 'packet_length', 'padding_length', 'payload', and 'random padding' MUST be a multiple of the cipher block size or 8, whichever is larger.  This constraint MUST be enforced, even when using stream ciphers. 

I don't know if a later RFC relaxed that restriction, but indeed OpenSSH does not seem to follow that.
!20188 should eliminate the extra sequence number tracking that you're doing. All you should need to do is make sure that the new secrets are generated.

Thanks !!   
To be more precise, all that tracking have nothing to do with decryption / rekey engine itself as it's not needed in first pass, I added this to be able to restore the encryption context of each frames while Wireshark UI pass again on the frames (due to Wireshark UI design).   
I'm sorry I can't test your last MR tonight, I'm testing tomorrow morning (CET) and going back here    
 
NB: I totally stopped calling ssh_dissect_key_exchange() from ssh_dissect_decrypted_packet() and except the packet length issue on rekey NEWKEYS, all other parsing for msg_code 20,30 and 31 are OK now in the rekey context (without any expert_info warnings)    
Thanks for last advice!

There is only msg_code NEWKEYS which had an expert_info after REKEY due to the fact OpenSSH seems to violate the specs on decrypted packet length if RFC is also valid for decrypted packet length (not sure of this but since last answer, I didn't find any RFC update or draft (maybe I didn't search enough...) regarding this point).  

Dissector apply RFC strictly so I'm not the good one to decide if we must break it or not  

The idea could be tracking a NEWKEYS frame (to bemore precise a NEWKEYS message in a frame including several messages and msg_code which is less trivial) and when detecting this message in a frame, execute a routine which break RFC compliant check and allow payload to be as small as msg_code field in a total of 12 bytes including the length prefix of value 8)

### So as a result, ... Yes OpenSSH is violating RFC4253 

In fact it's due to the stream cipher chacha20-poly1305 which is concider to have a block size of 1 => which must be a multiple of 8 (from RFC4253)      

But OpenSSH assume this choice (Damien Miller himself commited: https://lists.mindrot.org/pipermail/openssh-unix-dev/2013-December/031865.html)     

Also see:    
https://blog.djm.net.au/2013/11/chacha20-and-poly1305-in-openssh.html     

And   
https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/master/PROTOCOL.chacha20poly1305     



The total packet length (without prefix) which is a multiple of 12 seems to be a rest of block ciphers and we can find in OpenSSH    code:      
```c
block_size = enc ? enc->block_size : 8;
```    
https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/2827b6ac304ded8f99e8fbc12e7299133fadb2c2/packet.c#L1183    

and    
```c
	padlen = block_size - (len % block_size);
	if (padlen < 4)
		padlen += block_size;
```
    
https://github.com/openssh/openssh-portable/blob/2827b6ac304ded8f99e8fbc12e7299133fadb2c2/packet.c#L1221-L1223    

Now for ChaCha20-Poly1305, the block_size is effectively 1, since it's a stream cipher (no block alignment needed).    
    
   
So from my understanding, **OpenSSH is voluntary violating RFC4253** (for performance or simplicity reason ?) and a justification could be:   
- ChaCha20 is a stream cipher - it doesn't require alignment
- The real-world consequence of the rule in RFC 4253 doesn’t apply to AEAD modes like ChaCha20-Poly1305   
- OpenSSH defines the cipher in a way that "effectively reinterprets" the padding/alignment rules for AEAD modes   
- This was acknowledged and justified in the design of chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com.    

It's beeing conform with this document too:   
https://github.com/rus-cert/ssh-chacha20-poly1305-drafts/blob/master/ssh-chacha20-poly1305%40openssh.md#padding   

So maybe opening an issue here at Wireshark / TShark and making a MR to purpose change of the `12 bytes length` length check when an AEAD cipher like chacha20-poly1305@openssh.com is used could be a good and year 2025 aligned idea ?

The line in OpenSSH that changes the behavior with ChaCha20 and some other ciphers is the previous one:

`len -= aadlen; /* packet length is not encrypted for EtM modes */`

> The total packet length (without prefix) which is a multiple of 12 seems to be a rest of block ciphers and we can find in OpenSSH code

I don't understand your sentence here (especially the use of "to be a rest"; in any case, it's not that the total packet length is a multiple of 12, but that the total packet length is fixed to be 4 mod 8; the padding length is chosen so that the total packet length not including the packet_length field is a multiple of 8, and then the packet_length field is added.

The same issue is somewhat more directly addressed by [RFC 5647](https://datatracker.ietf.org/doc/html/rfc5647#section-7.3), which describes AES-GCM in SSH. In AES-GCM the packet length is not encrypted at all, and treated as AAD. In that case, it's clear that the overall length is going to be 4 mod 16 and not a multiple of 8 (contra RFC 4253), but RFC 5647 specifically addresses that. Furthermore, since the block size of AES is 16, the other restrictions of RFC 4253 are satisfied, e.g., the length is always greater than the minimum 16.

The current I-D of ChaCha20 handling in Secure Shell does not mention the incompatibility. In addition, as its a stream cipher, it would be possible to comply with RFC 4253 and include the packet_length field (which is, incidentally, encrypted if by a different cipher) when deciding how much padding to include. That contrasts with AES-GCM, where the total encrypted length must be 4 mod 16 and there's no way around it.

In any case, the length check as currently implemented only adds an expert info warning to the tree and does not prevent decryption and dissection.
And the warning doesn't particularly have to do with this merge request, so we can consider it later.
